svg.text: Receipts Engine, level 2: Concurrency & Atomic Numbering
Deep-dive into postgres row locking under high concurrency (20 simultaneous payments) and rollback atomicity.
Concurrent Numbering Execution
Problem: 20 Simultaneous Payments in 1 Organization
If two transactions read SELECT MAX(number), both see BM-2026-000005 and collide on unique constraint.
Gapless guarantee: No skipped numbers (000001, 000002... 000020) allowed under any concurrency.
Solution: PostgreSQL Row-Level Lock on receipt_counters
INSERT INTO receipt_counters (org_id, year, last_seq)
VALUES ($1, $2, 1)
ON CONFLICT (org_id, year) DO UPDATE
SET last_seq = receipt_counters.last_seq + 1 RETURNING last_seq;
Postgres queues each transaction on the row lock; each gets a unique, strictly incrementing integer.
Verified by Test: 20 Parallel supertest Promises
`await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: 20 }).map(() => record({ amountPoisha: 100 })))`
Result: numbers sorted match exactly BM-2026-000001 through BM-2026-000020.
Zero 409 conflicts, zero deadlocks, zero skipped sequence numbers.
Year Boundary Roll-Over:
Primary Key is composite (org_id, year). On Jan 1 2027, the counter inserts a fresh row
starting at BM-2027-000001, isolated cleanly per organization.
Transaction Atomicity & Rollback
Test Scenario: Receipt Insertion Failure Simulation
Trigger on receipts table throws an exception: `RAISE EXCEPTION 'receipt insert failed'`
Simulates database disk full, foreign key failure, or connection drop right at the final step.
All Prior Operations in $tx Are Rolled Back:
• Payment record creation: ROLLED BACK (count = 0)
• Rule 5 payment_allocations: ROLLED BACK (count = 0)
• Overpayment credit_entries: ROLLED BACK (count = 0)
• receipt_counters row / seq: ROLLED BACK (count = 0)
• Bill status update (reverts to 'issued', paid_poisha = 0)
Outbox Event Safety:
• Outbox table is written inside the very same $tx
`SELECT payload FROM outbox WHERE org_id = ... AND type = 'payment.confirmed'`
Asserted in test: exactly 0 outbox events! No ghost notifications sent.
Financial Invariant Guaranteed:
Either the entire payment, allocations, receipt, and credit commit together, or none of them do.
